topic: What if you fail the exam?
title_jp: もし{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちたら？
context: Tuesday: アルちゃん's first day helping in the English class at 鷹ノ原高校. 佐藤先生 introduces him, and the class does a 'what if…' question time. A 2nd-year student, 澪, nervous about next year's entrance exams, asks him the question she really cares about.

phrases.jp: もし{生まれ変わったら|うまれかわったら|to be reborn|3}、{何|なに}になりたい？
phrases.en: If you were reborn, what would you want to be?
phrases.note: A classic 'what if' question between friends. もし just warns 'a hypothesis is coming'; 〜たら does the real work.

phrases.jp: {私|わたし}だったら、{先生|せんせい}に{相談|そうだん|asking for advice|4}すると{思|おも}います。
phrases.en: If it were me, I think I'd ask a teacher for advice.
phrases.note: {私|わたし}だったら = 'if I were you': the gentlest way to give advice without telling someone what to do.

phrases.jp: {来月|らいげつ}、{東京|とうきょう}に{引っ越す|ひっこす|to move house|4}ことになりました。
phrases.en: It's been decided that I'm moving to Tokyo next month.
phrases.note: The standard way to announce news at work or school: ことになりました makes it sound decided by circumstances, not just by you.

phrases.jp: {試験|しけん}に{受かったら|うかったら|to pass (an exam)|3}、{何|なに}する？
phrases.en: What will you do if you pass the exam?
phrases.note: Spoken: {受|う}かる. Written and formal: {合格|ごうかく}する. The opposite is {落|お}ちる.

phrases.jp: {修学旅行|しゅうがくりょこう|school trip|3}、どこに{泊まった|とまった|to stay overnight|4}の？
phrases.en: Where did you stay on your school trip?
phrases.note: Almost every Japanese adult has a 修学旅行 story (often Kyoto or Nara): an easy small-talk question.

dialogue_setting: Classroom 2-3 at 鷹ノ原高校, 4th period English. 佐藤先生 at the front, アルちゃん beside her, 30 students staring at him.

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: みなさん、{今日|きょう}から{毎週|まいしゅう}{火曜日|かようび}に、アルちゃんが{授業|じゅぎょう|class, lesson|4}を{手伝って|てつだって|to help|4}くれることになりました。{今日|きょう}は「もし〜たら」の{質問|しつもん}タイムです。どうぞ。
dialogue.en: Everyone, from today アルちゃん will be helping with our class every Tuesday. Today is 'what if…' question time. Go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: あの、{質問|しつもん}してもいいですか。もし{日本|にほん}の{高校生|こうこうせい}だったら、{部活|ぶかつ|school club|4}は{何|なに}に{入りますか|はいりますか|to join|4}？
dialogue.en: Um, may I ask something? If you were a Japanese high-school student, which club would you join?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: うーん、もし{入れる|はいれる}なら、{吹奏楽部|すいそうがくぶ|brass band club|2}かな。{楽器|がっき|musical instrument|3}は{何|なに}もできないけど…。
dialogue.en: Hmm, if I could join, the brass band, I guess. Though I can't play any instrument…

dialogue.speaker: 澪
dialogue.jp: え、{ガチ||(slang) = 本当, seriously|3}ですか！{私|わたし}、{吹奏楽部|すいそうがくぶ|brass band club|2}でトランペット{吹いて|ふいて|to blow, play (wind instrument)|3}ます！…じゃあ、もし{試験|しけん}に{落ちたら|おちたら|to fail (an exam)|4}、どうしますか？{私|わたし}、{来年|らいねん}{受験|じゅけん|taking entrance exams|3}なんで…。
dialogue.en: Wait, seriously? I play trumpet in the brass band! …OK, then: what would you do if you failed an exam? I've got entrance exams next year, so…
dialogue.note: ガチ is teen slang for 本当に / マジ. Teens drop it into polite speech too: ガチですか.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {僕|ぼく}も{前|まえ}に{試験|しけん}に{落ちた|おちた|to fail (an exam)|4}ことがあるよ。でも、もう{一回|いっかい}がんばって、{結局|けっきょく|in the end|4}{日本|にほん}に{来る|くる}ことになった。{落ちても|おちても}、{終わり|おわり}じゃないよ。
dialogue.en: I've failed an exam before too. But I tried again, and in the end it turned out I came to Japan. Failing isn't the end.

dialogue.speaker: 佐藤先生
dialogue.jp: いいお{話|はなし}ですね。じゃあ{澪|みお}さん、もし{東京|とうきょう}の{大学|だいがく}に{合格|ごうかく|passing (an exam)|3}したら、{何|なに}がしたいですか。{英語|えいご}で{答えて|こたえて}みましょう。
dialogue.en: What a nice story. So, 澪さん: if you get into a university in Tokyo, what do you want to do? Let's try answering in English.

grammar.meaning: it's been decided that / it turns out that
grammar.form: {辞書形|じしょけい}: + ことになる ({手伝|てつだ}う → {手伝|てつだ}うことになる, {来|く}る → {来|く}ることになる) · ない{形|けい}: + ことになる ({行|い}かない → {行|い}かないことになる) · announcement: ことになりました ({引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すことになりました)
grammar.explanation: Use it when something was decided by someone else or by circumstances, or simply 'turned out' that way: the speaker presents it as an outcome, not a personal choice. Its partner 〜ことにする (taught last lesson) is 'I decided'. Japanese often prefer ことになりました even for their own decisions, because it sounds modest: 'it has come about that…'.

examples.jp: {来週|らいしゅう}から{夜|よる}のシフトに{入る|はいる}ことになった。
examples.en: It's been decided I'll do night shifts from next week.

examples.jp: {雨|あめ}のため、{運動会|うんどうかい|sports day|3}は{中止|ちゅうし|cancelled|3}することになりました。
examples.en: Because of the rain, sports day has been cancelled.

quiz.question: {会社|かいしゃ}の{命令|めいれい|order (from above)|3}で、{来月|らいげつ}{大阪|おおさか}に＿＿ことになった。
quiz.en: On the company's orders, I'm to go to Osaka next month.
quiz.explain: ことになる takes the dictionary form, even for future events; the past goes on なる (なった). And because the company decided, it's ことになる, not ことにする.

mark: 手伝ってくれることになりました
引っ越すことになりました
中止することになりました

quiz_more.question: {会議|かいぎ}の{結果|けっか|result|4}、{新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}を{出|だ}す＿＿。
quiz_more.en: After the meeting, it was decided that we'll open a new shop.
quiz_more.explain: Decided by the meeting, not by you alone: ことになった. ことにした sounds like your own personal choice.

quiz_more.question: {来月|らいげつ}から、{寮|りょう|dormitory|3}に＿＿ことになりました。
quiz_more.en: From next month, I'll be living in the dorm (it's been arranged).
quiz_more.explain: ことになる follows the dictionary form: 住むことになった.

kanji.where: The sign on a door in every Japanese high school: where students talk with teachers about exams, university and jobs.
kanji.related: {進路|しんろ} = your path after school; {受験生|じゅけんせい} = a student taking entrance exams.
kanji.breakdown: {進路指導室|しんろしどうしつ}: 進路 path ahead (進 advance + 路 road) + 指導 guidance + 室 room → 'the room where they guide your path'.

tip.title: Words you don't say to a 受験生
tip.body: Around students preparing for entrance exams, people avoid 落ちる (to fall/fail) and すべる (to slip, slang for failing): even dropping something becomes a bad omen. Instead they give lucky things: a 合格お{守|まも}り from a shrine, or a KitKat, because キットカット sounds like きっと{勝|か}つ, 'you'll surely win'. 澪 asked the question herself, so アルちゃん's honest 落ちた was fine.

challenge.prompt: {澪|みお}, back in Japanese: 「アルちゃん、もしスペインに{帰る|かえる}ことになったら、{日本|にほん}の{何|なに}が{一番|いちばん}{恋しく|こいしく|to miss, long for|3}なると{思|おも}いますか？」 Answer her (politely, it's class) and say what you'd miss most.
challenge.hint: もし〜ことになったら · 〜が{一番|いちばん}{恋|こい}しくなる · 〜と{思|おも}います
challenge.model_answer: もしスペインに{帰る|かえる}ことになったら、{田中|たなか}さんのりんごが{一番|いちばん}{恋しく|こいしく|to miss, long for|3}なると{思|おも}います。
challenge.explanation: {帰|かえ}ることになったら = 'if it turns out I have to go back': ことになる (not your choice) inside a 〜たら condition. {恋|こい}しい + なる = 'come to miss'. です・ます because you're speaking in front of the class.

vocab.note: A class you attend. The subject itself is {科目|かもく}.
Short for {部活動|ぶかつどう}. Clubs train almost every day, weekends too: a big part of school life.

vocab.en: to blow; to play (a wind instrument)
vocab.note: Also used for wind: {風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}く. Piano and guitar use {弾|ひ}く instead.
{試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちる = to fail an exam. Opposite: {受|う}かる.
{受験生|じゅけんせい} = a student in exam year. A whole season of Japanese life.
{合格|ごうかく}する = to pass. On notices you'll see {合格発表|ごうかくはっぴょう}: the day results are posted.

extras.intro: Words every Japanese teenager uses, and you'll hear in the staff room.

items.note: Usually in the 2nd year of high school.

{先輩|せんぱい|senior (at school or work)|4}・{後輩|こうはい|junior|3}
items.note: Decided by year, not age; club life runs on it.

extras.title: Ways to say 'what if'
extras.intro: Four conditionals you'll hear, from most everyday to most 'imaginary'.

items.jp: {雨|あめ}だったら、{行|い}かない。
items.en: If it rains, I won't go.

items.note: 〜なら: reacting to what someone else said or plans.

items.en: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

items.jp: {宝|たから}くじが{当|あ}たったとしたら？
